$comment: Inverted truthfulness check. A page can contain no false sentence and still mislead by omitting a limitation we know exists. Every entry must cite verifiedBy: how we know the limitation is real. Never add an entry from memory alone.

caveats.why: Safari support is macOS only and needs the full Xcode app, and preview and start have no Safari path. A reader who skips this plans a workflow the toolchain cannot run.
caveats.verifiedBy: measured on macOS 26.5.2, Safari 26.5.2 and Xcode 26.6 for the Safari session work merged as 0508e40cd; extension build --help: 'safari builds a Safari app via Xcode (macOS only)'. The earlier 'no live reload' half of this caveat was deleted because a save now reloads the extension in Safari.

caveats.why: An unguarded Chromium-only call at the top level of a background script throws on Safari, Safari discards the background context, and the developer gets no logs, no reload and no error. Without this callout a silent Safari session reads as a toolchain bug.
caveats.verifiedBy: measured on macOS 26.5.2, Safari 26.5.2 and Xcode 26.6 during the Safari session work merged as 0508e40cd; the build-time API warnings added in that commit exist to catch this case

caveats.why: A content script with world set to MAIN runs in the page's own JavaScript world only from Chrome 111, Firefox 128 and Safari 18, and it has no extension APIs there. A reader who misses the versions ships to a browser that ignores the key, and a reader who misses the API limit calls chrome.runtime from a script that does not have it.
caveats.verifiedBy: mdn/browser-compat-data webextensions/manifest/content_scripts.json, world: Chrome 111, Firefox 128, Safari 18, no partial notes, read 2026-11-11. Observed build: a production build loaded in a managed headless Firefox Nightly 158 ran the world: MAIN manifest content script in the page's own world under manifest_version 2 and manifest_version 3 (it read a page-owned global and had no browser.runtime), while the plain entry ran isolated. The earlier 'Chromium only' form of this caveat was deleted because Firefox 128 and Safari 18 honor the key.

anyOf: headless[^\n]{0,60}(extensions are not|does not support|drops|will not load)
caveats.why: The page's example sets headless: false with no explanation. Playwright's default headless mode runs headless_shell, which silently loads no extensions, so a reader adapting the snippet for CI gets a green run that tested nothing.
caveats.verifiedBy: Playwright chromium headless_shell does not support extensions; verified in this project while building the visual-render and reload suites, which require headless: false plus --headless=new
